LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. Despite a three-game winning streak earlier this season and a 4-3 record overall, the Packers are in last place in the NFC North heading into Week 8. So, every game means a ton for Jordan Love, Matt LaFleur and Co. as they look to get back to the playoffs. Bryce Young and the Panthers are in a different spot, as they’re in first place in the weak NFC South despite going 3-3 through their first six games. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. Still, oddsmakers aren’t expecting them to have another blowout loss with this spread set inside a touchdown on Thursday. All week long, the SI Betting team has shared our favorite game picks, props, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more for Panthers vs. Packers. Packers running back Josh Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but he returned in Week 7 and made an immediate impact against the Detroit Lions. Jacobs played just 52.2 percent of Green Bay’s offense snaps, but he saw 18 opportunities (11 rushes, seven targets) and ended up finding the end zone. So, the volume should be there against a Carolina defense that is pretty average against the pass (13th in EPA/Pass) this season. I think Golden is undervalued at this number in Week 8. away.headline: Panthers' concerns going into Thursday's game against the Packers just got even worse based on the final Week 8 injury report
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers had a lot of concerns going into this week after the beatdown the team suffered on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. To make things even harder, the Panthers had a short turnaround to make adjustments with a road trip coming up on Thursday against the Green Bay Packers. That already was going to be a rough road matchup for this team with everything going on coming out of the last game, and to make things even worse, the team's final Week 8 injury report added even more concerns. First off, the Panthers have officially ruled out star pass rusher Jaelan Phillips for the second consecutive game with a hamstring injury. Given the nature of the injury, the fact it's a reaggravation, and this being a short week, it was always unlikely that Phillips would have been able to play against the Packers. Wednesday's injury report confirmed those suspicions, leaving the Panthers without their top edge rusher. Being without Phillips really hurt the Panthers last week. Tampa Bay exposed the Panthers in the run game attacking the edges with counters and rumbled for over 250 yards on the ground. It was an embarrassing performance and not having Phillips out there to set the edge was a big reason for it, along with poor tackling. Big picture, sitting Phillips is the right call for him. He needs to get that hamstring figured out before rushing back into action like he did in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which is what caused this injury to reaggravate in the first place. The Panthers need Phillips for the long haul and need him fully healthy before returning. Another notable injury designation is left guard Damien Lewis, who will be out for Thursday's game due to a knee injury. Lewis was easily the team's best offensive lineman, allowing seven pressures this season on over 200 pass blocking snaps. The other four starters have each allowed 15+ pressures this season. The Panthers are also without backup guard Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) and elevated Jake Curhan from the practice squad as a result. The Panthers also placed veteran right tackle Taylor Moton on the injured reserve earlier this week after he fractured his fibula along with further damage to his ankle. That leaves Monroe Freeling to fill back in at right tackle, which in turn forces Rasheed Walker to remain at left tackle. Those two have allowed a combined five sacks and 42 pressures. In Lewis place at left guard, the Panthers will likely turn to Corey Bullock, who's played 71 pass blocking snaps this season with one sack and five pressures allowed. It's a tough look for quarterback Bryce Young, who has been having to overcome pressure all season long. One more worrisome injury to note is in the secondary. Akayleb Evans will not play either due to a triceps/knee injury. Evans has been filling in as a starter, and largely has struggled, in place of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. home.headline: Packers make late add to injury report, list CB Keisean Nixon as questionable
home.blurb: Packers make late add to injury report, list CB Keisean Nixon as questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Packers make late add to injury report, list CB Keisean Nixon as questionable The Green Bay Packers added cornerback Keisean Nixon to the injury report before Thursday night's showdown with the Carolina Panthers . The team says Nixon is questionable to play with a shoulder injury. Nixon joins four other questionable players for the Packers: receiver Matthew Golden (foot/shoulder), defensive linemen Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr. (quad). Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and right guard Travis Glover (knee) have all been ruled out for Thursday night. Not having Nixon available on Thursday night would push either Carrington Valentine or Benjamin St-Juste into the starting lineup opposite rookie Brandon Cisse. St-Juste is expected to return after missing two games with a hamstring injury. Kamal Hadden is also available at corner. He has not missed a game since joining the Packers before the 2022 season, appearing in all 75 regular season games. Nixon started the first seven games of the 2026 season as the defense's left cornerback. The Packers defense is about to face ascending young receiver Tetairoa McMillan, who ranks 11th in the NFL in receiving yards entering Week 8. Gameday inactives are due for the Packers and Panthers at around 5:45 p.m. CT.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. Fresh off their bye week, the Bills are looking to pick up where they left off offensively, but hope to find more success on defense. It won't be easy since they will be facing a strong Ravens team, which will be getting a boost thanks to the return of quarterback Lamar Jackson. After missing three games with a high ankle sprain, Jackson is expected to make his way back to the field against the Bills. That means both teams will have their MVP quarterbacks on the field and the last time they met was in Week 1 of the 2025 season. Josh Allen led the Bills to a remarkable comeback victory, with Matt Prater drilling a field goal as time expired to give Buffalo a 41-40 win. This weekend, there should be plenty of fireworks once again, but who do the experts believe will come away with the win. Let's look around at some of the main media outlets to find out that answer. Both of these AFC teams are contenders to win the Super Bowl this season, and the Ravens are expected to get Lamar Jackson back in action after he missed three games with a sprained ankle. The Ravens won just one of the three games that Jackson missed, and their offense has struggled over the last two weeks in losses against AFC North opponents in Cleveland and Cincinnati. The Ravens don't want to fall back to .500 this season, and they're set as small underdogs on the road against Buffalo. With every team in the AFC North sitting at over .500 this season, the Ravens can't afford too many more losses, especially against teams that they may be competing for a wild card spot against. Right now, the Bills are in first place in the AFC East, and they're coming off their bye week after a 5-1 start to the season. Josh Allen is the leading candidate to win the MVP award, and he's been terrific as both a passer and a runner. Now, he takes on a Baltimore defense that features Kyle Hamilton, Marlon Humphrey, Nate Wiggins and others in the secondary that could make it tough on a Buffalo passing game that has been short-handed at receiver for a lot of the season. The Bills are hoping to keep things rolling out of their bye, as they're two games up in the loss column on the New England Patriots in the AFC East. Oddsmakers have set Buffalo as a favorite at home, and there are several players on both of these teams that are worth a look in the prop market. So, ahead of this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made player prop picks, game picks, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more to help you wager on Bills vs. Ravens. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Ravens vs. Bills in Week 8 Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Baltimore Ravens +3.5 (-110) vs. Buffalo Bills – Iain MacMillan Josh Allen OVER 7.5 Rush Attempts (+106) – Peter Dewey Zay Flowers Anytime TD (+165) – Peter Dewey Ja’Kobi Lane OVER 2.5 Receptions (-134) – Peter Dewey Each week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . He’s taking the Ravens to cover with Jackson expected back in the lineup: Betting on this game hinges on whether or not Lamar Jackson is going to be able to suit up for the Ravens. Unfortunately, I place my bets early in the week, so I don't have the benefit of knowing whether or not the two-time MVP will be on the field on Sunday. The betting line indicates that he will, so I'm going to trust that, along with the reports that Jesse Minter is optimistic that Jackson will be ready to go. When a team only has one loss on their schedule, and they have the best quarterback in football on their roster, a lot of their issues are overlooked. That's the case for the Bills, whose defense has been horrendous this season, ranking 30th in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. They are the only defense in football that ranks in the bottom three in both of those metrics. I hesitate to lay more than a field goal on any team with that bad of a defense, especially when that defense potentially has to face another MVP candidate at quarterback. I'll take the points with Baltimore on Sunday. Allen has been awesome on the ground this season, carrying the ball 48 times (eight times per game) for 240 yards and eight scores. Allen is the preferred option for the Bills in short yardage, handling eight or more carries in three of his six games. Fresh out of a bye, I expect Allen to be as healthy as he’s been this season, which could be a good sign for him using his legs. The Ravens are allowing over four yards per carry to opposing quarterbacks, and Allen had 14 carries in the meeting between these teams during the 2025 regular season. Baltimore ranks 12th in the league in EPA/Rush, so the Bills and Joe Brady may get creative with the running game rather than riding James Cook (who has had fumbling issues) on Sunday. At plus money, this prop is worth a shot for the former league MVP. away.headline: Game Recap: Ravens Blown Out By Bills After Quarterback Injuries
away.blurb: Ravens Blown Out By Bills After Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley Leave With Injuries | Game Recap Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS In the second quarter, inside linebacker Roquan Smith knocked the ball out of Bills wideout DJ Moore's grasp, and the fumble was recovered by T.J. Tampa, who was playing in his first game since suffering a knee injury in Week 1. It was Smith's second forced fumble of the season and Tampa's first career fumble recovery. news Game Recap: Ravens Blow Out Colts in Season Opener Quentin Corpuel Editorial Associate The Ravens suffers a third straight loss Sunday in Buffalo and perhaps more than that. Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive play and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley went down in the second quarter with a toe injury, thrusting undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. Baltimore's defense played an inspired game, but the Ravens ultimately lost, 36-10, against the Bills. When Jackson is on the field, the Ravens have usually been one of the NFL's best offenses. When he's off the field, the Ravens have been far from the top. Jackson's quick exit on Sunday was a game changer. In his first career regular-season appearance, Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards with interception and lost fumble. Fagnano and Huntley were under siege often, as the Bills were credited with four sacks and 12 quarterback hits. The last time three quarterbacks appeared in a regular-season game for the Ravens was Nov. 26, 2000. Baltimore is the first team to have three quarterbacks throw a pass before halftime of a game since the 2017 Dallas Cowboys, per ESPN’s Jamison Hensley . The Ravens had just 52 yards of offense in the first half and 144 for the game. The Bills piled up 426 yards. Zay Flowers entered the game as one of the NFL's leading receivers but had zero receptions in a game for the first time in his career. Justice Hill led the Ravens in catches with four that went for 20 yards. Rashod Bateman's 22-yard reception early in the third quarter was enough to lead the Ravens in receiving yards. One week after allowing 35 points in the second half against the Cincinnati Bengals, Baltimore's defense came to play in the first half against Buffalo. After the Bills opened the game with a 10-play, 60-yard touchdown drive, they scored just nine points the rest of the half on three field goals by Tyler Bass. Two of them came after Buffalo forced turnovers and started the ensuing offensive drive on Baltimore's 20- and 33-yard lines. Defensive lineman Broderick Washington Jr. secured his first career interception on after Bills tight end bobbled a pass from Allen straight up in the air. It was Baltimore's first takeaway since Week 5. The Ravens capitalized on Washington's interception, as Derrick Henry scored a 2-yard rushing touchdown on the ensuing drive. It was Henry's first rushing touchdown since Week 4, and Henry is now tied with Marshall Faulk for the seventh-most rushing touchdowns in NFL

home.blurb: Ravens Blown Out By Bills After Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley Leave With Injuries | Game Recap Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS In the second quarter, inside linebacker Roquan Smith knocked the ball out of Bills wideout DJ Moore's grasp, and the fumble was recovered by T.J. Tampa, who was playing in his first game since suffering a knee injury in Week 1. It was Smith's second forced fumble of the season and Tampa's first career fumble recovery. news Game Recap: Ravens Blow Out Colts in Season Opener Quentin Corpuel Editorial Associate The Ravens suffers a third straight loss Sunday in Buffalo and perhaps more than that. Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive play and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley went down in the second quarter with a toe injury, thrusting undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. Baltimore's defense played an inspired game, but the Ravens ultimately lost, 36-10, against the Bills. When Jackson is on the field, the Ravens have usually been one of the NFL's best offenses. When he's off the field, the Ravens have been far from the top. Jackson's quick exit on Sunday was a game changer. In his first career regular-season appearance, Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards with interception and lost fumble. Fagnano and Huntley were under siege often, as the Bills were credited with four sacks and 12 quarterback hits. The last time three quarterbacks appeared in a regular-season game for the Ravens was Nov. 26, 2000. Baltimore is the first team to have three quarterbacks throw a pass before halftime of a game since the 2017 Dallas Cowboys, per ESPN’s Jamison Hensley . The Ravens had just 52 yards of offense in the first half and 144 for the game. The Bills piled up 426 yards. Zay Flowers entered the game as one of the NFL's leading receivers but had zero receptions in a game for the first time in his career. Justice Hill led the Ravens in catches with four that went for 20 yards. Rashod Bateman's 22-yard reception early in the third quarter was enough to lead the Ravens in receiving yards. One week after allowing 35 points in the second half against the Cincinnati Bengals, Baltimore's defense came to play in the first half against Buffalo. After the Bills opened the game with a 10-play, 60-yard touchdown drive, they scored just nine points the rest of the half on three field goals by Tyler Bass. Two of them came after Buffalo forced turnovers and started the ensuing offensive drive on Baltimore's 20- and 33-yard lines. Defensive lineman Broderick Washington Jr. secured his first career interception on after Bills tight end bobbled a pass from Allen straight up in the air. It was Baltimore's first takeaway since Week 5. The Ravens capitalized on Washington's interception, as Derrick Henry scored a 2-yard rushing touchdown on the ensuing drive. It was Henry's first rushing touchdown since Week 4, and Henry is now tied with Marshall Faulk for the seventh-most rushing touchdowns in NFL

Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. My Titans vs. Bengals prediction is the Over 46.5 after the Titans traded All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears on Thursday, leaving the Bengals 11.5-point favorites this afternoon. The Titans' defense was already last in DVOA at FTN before losing its anchor up front, while the Bengals are coming off a 35-13 win over the Ravens. TOP PICK Titans vs Bengals prediction: Over 46.5 One of my first plays of Week 8 was taking the Over in this game. And with Jeffery Simmons swapping his trademark red sleeves for Chicago orange in a deal that has the Bears surging up the Super Bowl odds board , I like the Over even more, considering the Cincinnati Bengals will do the heavy lifting. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Ravens stop unit in the second half of last week's win. They finished with 7.0 yards per play and were a perfect 5 for 5 in the red zone, with Joe Burrow and his talented receiving corps finding their stride. The Titans' secondary allows the second-highest completion rate and has been burned by multiple big plays, bleeding the fourth-most passes of 20+ yards entering Week 8. While they haven't given up many passing touchdowns, they haven't faced many QBs on Burrow's level. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring, but don't discount the Titans. They're playing with pace and face a Bengals defense that still has work to do. Our Week 8 SGP roundup features a Titans vs. Bengals combo as well. Chase Brown finds the end zone to the cheers of fantasy owners everywhere. He faces a watered-down Titans defense that's allowed six scores to running backs. Tee Higgins ' projections call for as many as 91 yards against a Titans secondary giving up explosive plays. Chase Brown anytime touchdown Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Titans vs Bengals touchdown scorer: Chase Brown If anyone was happy to see Simmons traded before Week 8, it was Bengals running back Brown. He no longer has to worry about one of the premier run stoppers in the game, facing a Titans red-zone defense now missing its biggest cog. Even when Simmons was in the mix, the Titans had allowed six scores to rival RBs. Brown has only one touchdown in 2026 despite 13 carries and three receptions in the red zone. Due to that drought, we're getting a discount on his anytime touchdown market in Week 8, considering this prop was trading around 60% two games ago. Given the massive spread, the Bengals will be in a run-positive game script in the second half on Sunday, helping boost Brown's TD probabilities. His TD forecasts range between 60% and 78%, given he's a threat to run one in or catch a touchdown pass. For other options, browse our Week 8 anytime touchdown picks . Titans vs Bengals player prop: Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards The Bengals have arguably the best one-two punch at receiver in the NFL, with Higgins serving as Robin to Ja'Marr Chase 's Batman. Just don't tell Higgins that. He looked more like Superman in Week 7, putting in a monster effort in the win over the rival Ravens. He caught six of seven balls his way for 148 yards and a touchdown. That includes a 44-yard dinger on a broken play with Burrow dodging pressure. We mentioned the Titans' problems giving up home runs over the top, and Higgins is one of the best deep threats in the land, averaging 21.6 air yards per reception and amassing eight catches for 20+ yards. The Titans have also been burned by WR2s to start the season, ranking 24th in DVOA vs. WR2s at FTN while giving up almost 56 yards per game to those second options. Higgins' Week 8 models are very bullish on his receiving yards, ranging from 65 to a high of 91. Most forecasts come in above 80 yards, and my projection sits just shy of 81 yards receiving. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Bengals are 13.5-point favorites over the Titans on the spread, with the total set at over/under 45.5 points. Cincinnati is a -950 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tennessee is a +640 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs Bengals predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 1. Titans vs Bengals pick: Bengals -13.5 (-110) My Bengals vs. Titans best bet is Cincinnati to cover the spread. Titans vs Bengals NFL Odds Titans vs Bengals spread : Titans +13.5 (-110), Titans -13.5 (-110) Titans vs Bengals total : over/under 45.5 (-118o / 104u) Titans vs Bengals moneyline : Titans +640, Bengals -950 Titans vs Bengals Preview for NFL Week 8 Tennessee Titans Preview: Life Without Jeffery Simmons Fading the Titans has been a profitable endeavor this year, but they have covered the number in each of their last two road games. I provided the breakdown for their victory on the road in Indianapolis and their road cover as 11-point underdogs in Baltimore back in Week 4. I will not be going back to the well for a third time in this spot against the Bengals as too many factors are working against them. For starters, the Titans traded away their best defensive player this week in Jeffery Simmons and will also be without leading receiver in Carnell Tate. Opposing running backs have averaged four yards per carry against Tennessee with Simmons on the field — that number increases to 4.5 yards per carry on the 35 carries he has not been in the lineup. The Titans' explosive rush rate allowed also increases from 9.8% with Simmons to 14.3% without Simmons on the field. Simmons boasts the fifth-highest pass rush grade this season out of all defensive tackles , per Pro Football Focus. The lack of interior pressure will allow Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to build upon his red-hot finish to Week 7. Burrow was surgical in the second half versus Baltimore, completing 88% of his passes for an average of 13.8 yards per attempt. Burrow is heating up, as he historically does as the season progresses — and now, he gets a highly exploitable matchup. Tennessee's defense under head coach Robert Saleh ranks 31st in completion percentage allowed and 27th in yards per attempt allowed. The Titans' pressure rate of 30.6% ranks 26th. However, it is even more concerning when looking at the time charted to get those pressures on quarterbacks. The Titans' 2.8 seconds per pressure is the worst in the NFL, and that number is almost certainly going to get worse with the loss of Simmons. If Tennessee is going to make this game competitive, it has to be the doing of Cam Ward. Tony Pollard and the running game were excellent a week ago versus Cleveland, but the Bengals have the most improved run defense in the league. Cincinnati Bengals Preview: Good Spot for Cincy's Defense Al Golden's defense plays with the highest rate of light boxes in alignment, yet still leads the NFL in stuff rate defending running games. Golden can opt to add an extra defender on early downs to stymie Pollard, which will force Ward into long down-and-distance situations. Without their top weapon on the outside in Tate, the Titans lack playmakers to move the chains when they get to third down. Ward and company already struggle in these situations, ranking 27th in third-down conversion rate. The Bengals boast the eighth-best defense per dropback, according to expected points added (EPA). Projecting the Titans' success in this spot becomes extremely difficult when you consider that 43% of all their pass attempts on 2nd-and-8+ and 28% of all attempts on 3rd- or 4th-and-8+ longer were funneled to Tate. The Titans' passing game is facing an uphill battle in overcoming their deficiencies when their running game on standard downs isn't keeping them ahead of schedule. Titans vs Bengals Picks, Betting Analysis Tennessee has a -62 scoring margin in the first half of games this season, which is the worst in the league. The Titans will likely fall behind early and have no choice but to abandon the running game. This further puts the onus of any potential comeback in the hands of Cam Ward. Ward's 27.1 passer rating under pressure and turnover-worthy throw rate nearly doubling his big-time throw rate makes it too difficult to trust him in delivering any chance at a backdoor cover. The Bengals are -6.5 in the 1st half, which is another position worth a look. However, I am more comfortable allowing the full 60 minutes to play out as Ward's game-altering mistake(s) can come at any time. Joe Burrow is heating up at the right time and the Titans do not have the personnel to slow him down. I expect the Bengals to cruise to victory with significant margin. away.headline: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans
away.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. home.headline: Injury Report: Week 8 vs Cowboys
home.blurb: The Cardinals had been cautious with the rookie running back, but after three practices, the coaching staff felt Love was healthy enough to return. "Even though he's he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys by November 1st are truly at 100 (percent)," coach Mike LaFleur said. "But he's feeling as good as he can feel you know so yeah kind of go from there." Who will be blocking for him might be the bigger question. Center Hjalte Froholdt is questionable to play after being limited on Thursday with a knee injury. He did not practice on Friday. If unable to play, Hayden Conner could slide to center and the Cardinals would start a different player at right guard for the fourth time this season. Defensively, some reinforcements could be on the way. After missing the last three weeks, safety Dewey Wingard (knee) logged a full week of practice. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), are coming off a 16-10 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Meanwhile, Detroit defeated Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers a week ago, 20-17. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 8 matchup with Minnesota. Christian Booher The Lions have a chance to truly solidify themselves as division title contenders with a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Though the Vikings have underwhelmed offensively at times, they have found a way to start the season 6-0, thanks in part to a dominant defense that will be the best unit Detroit has faced to date. As a result, the pressure will be on Detroit's offense to come up with answers for a group that is led by one of the best defensive minds in football in Vikings coordinator Brian Flores. Jared Goff holds the key, as if he can get the ball out quickly and find answers within the opposition he will have a good chance to lead his group to a dominant performance. It's also an opportunity for the Lions' defense to make a statement against Kyler Murray. I think this game will feature turnovers on both sides, with the unit that gets the ball last ultimately finding a way to win. Detroit gets that advantage, as Goff leads Detroit to a game-winning field goal and a statement division victory. The Lions find a way to win ugly, and remind the league that they are capable of making a playoff run. Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Detroit Lions will face arguably their toughest test of the season yet when they square off with the undefeated Minnesota Vikings Sunday. The Vikings’ defense has been the definition of elite this season, allowing a measly 12.3 points per game (No. 1 in the NFL). You combine that with a stingy pass defense, and Lions signal-caller Jared Goff should have his hands full in the Week 8 affair. Plus, Detroit's defensive back and linebacker groups will need to bring their “A game” against Minnesota pass-catchers Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. It won't be easy for the Lions to emerge victorious in this divisional contest. However, I believe they will on the heels of strong efforts from their pass-rush and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. I believe that Gibbs will help seal the deal for Detroit with several key runs in the fourth quarter, ultimately setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning kick. Lions 24, Vikings 21 John Maakaron This is a game the Lions would ideally like to get out to an early lead, as the Vikings offense is far behind the defense. away.headline: Vikings-Lions Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR. away.headline: Jack Campbell Carted Off Field After Scary Injury for Lions vs. Vikings
away.blurb: He was transported to a local hospital, the team announced . On Monday, the Lions updated Campbell's condition, saying preliminary indications "are positive," but noted that "out of respect for Jack and his family" they would not share further information on his injury. Head coach Dan Campbell provided a limited update after the game: Needless to say, losing Campbell would be a significant blow to the Lions, who are 5-2 and looking to return to the playoffs after missing the playoffs last season. Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered what appears to be a serious injury during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. After making a tackle, Campbell was unable to get up on his own power and received attention from medical staff on the field before being carted off. Simmons Makes Bears Even Stronger 😤 Jack Campbell is one of the most important pieces of the Lions' defense, coming into Sunday's game leading the team in total tackles (54). He added three more tackles against the Vikings on Sunday before suffering his neck injury. He's coming off a season in which he earned a First-team All-Pro nod after collecting a career-high 176 tackles, five sacks and three forced fumbles. Detroit rewarded Campbell for his career season by giving him a four-year, $81 million contract extension over the offseason. The Lions selected Campbell with the 18th overall pick in 2023 after his standout career at Iowa. The 26-year-old has since developed not only into one of the best linebackers in the league, but also into the leader of Detroit's defense. "This is Jack Campbell's defense, and I don't hesitate when I say that," defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said of Campbell earlier this year. "This is Jack Campbell's defense and everyone in that locker room knows it. Point blank period. It all goes through Jack." 06:17 ▶️ Minshew Saves the Day TOP NEWS Bleacher Report • 3h Ravens Sign QB, Announce TNF Starter Bleacher Report • 1d Ranking Best Fan Traditions 🙌 Bleacher Report • 2h Bills Releasing CJGJ Bleacher Report • 1d New NFL Power Rankings 📊 Bleacher Report • 4h MLBPA Responds to Cap Proposal Bleacher Report • 11h Latest Mock Draft 📋 Bleacher Report • 3h Rivers Fave for NC State Job Bleacher Report • 8h Bron's Take on Injury Spike Bleacher Report • 7h Buzz: 'Multiple Teams' Eyeing Josh Sweat Bleacher Report • 4h LSU Honoring 'Bayou Barbie'

Neither team is looking too hot at the moment. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak and the Jets just lost to the previously winless Dolphins . To get a feel for how this one could play out, we get the takes from the Raiders Wire staff. Game picks for Raiders Week 8 matchup vs Jets Lance Fernandez -- Jets 24, Raiders 20 The Jets have struggled offensively, ranking in the bottom half in passing yards, rushing yards, and points per game. However, playing against a defense that has surrendered the fourth-most points per game and playing at home should give New York's offense a boost. That and the Jets' solid pass defense should keep the Raiders' losing streak going. Marvin Uzor -- Raiders 24, Jets 20 The Jets have been the NFL's slowest-starting offense since last season, so this is the week the Raiders finally don't have to dig out of an early hole. Put Kirk Cousins against a defense with one interception in 24 games, and I think the losing streak ends at four. Lamarr Fields -- Raiders 24. Jets 17 The Raiders will have some success running the ball and getting pressure on Geno Smith. Look for Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker to have good games. Levi Damien -- Raiders 20, Jets 19 Nothing about this Raiders team right now inspires confidence in me. And it isn't because they've lost four straight. It's the manner in which they lost them. Either just getting flat out streamrolled or giving up a ton of points and then trying to make a comeback when it's too late. The offensive line is starting to look like who we thought they were and the defense simply doesn't look smart. And playing on the east coast? Ugh. That being said, I have less confidence in Geno Smith. Perhaps that comes from the experience with him in Las Vegas last season, who knows. But I think the Jets record reflects that he's not the answer, with their only wins coming over a hapless Titans team and a low-scoring affair against the Browns. And they're coming off handing the Dolphins their first win of the season. The same Dolphins team the Raiders put a hurting on in the opener. I see a close one here. home.blurb: Bech, who has been on injured reserve with a broken right forearm since the Week 3 game against the New Orleans Saints, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game. Kubiak was asked if the wide receiver will be activated before the team's trek to the Big Apple, but the coach said they have until Saturday to make that decision, according to The Athletic's Sam Warren . In other Raiders injury news, backup edge defender Patrick Johnson (stinger) has been ruled out. That could lead to practice squad edge Cian Slone getting his third call-up in as many weeks. However, Slone has been a healthy scratch during the last two Sundays, and this would be his last call-up before the team has to add him to the 53-man roster if they want to elevate the undrafted rookie a fourth time. Guard Jackson Powers-Johnson (back) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice but was upgraded to limited on Friday and listed as questionable for Sunday. Bailey didn't practice at all during the week. Additionally, running back Breece Hall (quad) and offensive lineman/former Raider Dylan Parham (knee) are questionable. Hall was limited in practice all week, and Parham was limited for the first two sessions but was a full-go on Friday. The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production. Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward. If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards. Germie 100-Yard Game Incoming If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often. He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chris Pokorny · SB Nation Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:13 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns take on the Pittsburgh Steelers this Sunday. Both teams enter with the same record, but Cleveland has the division edge after beating Pittsburgh on Thursday Night Football earlier this season. The Steelers are undefeated at home, so are they looking to give medicine back to the Browns? Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 8 game between the Browns and Steelers: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Steelers: In their first meeting, the Browns' defense controlled the line of scrimmage, sacking Aaron Rodgers five times while piling up 10 total QB hits and keeping the veteran signal-caller all out of sorts. Things have turned a corner for the Steelers' offense in the last three weeks, with Rodgers playing in rhythm, limiting the giveaways and accurately finding his targets — though there's still a lot of pressure on rookie right tackle Max Iheanachor, who allowed two sacks and seven pressures (per NGS) against the Browns in Week 4. Everything about the 42-year-old quarterback's play has trended upward since their last meeting, and the rushing attack should flex its muscle more this time around with the return of Rico Dowdle. The Browns have rightfully earned their place at the top of the division through two months, but how long can they end up on the winning side of close games? We've seen this type of playing-with-fire approach before, and it rarely lasts. That said, watching this team get meaningful contributions from young players (Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, Spencer Fano, Carson Schwesinger) has been enjoyable and should keep Cleveland competitive should they maintain that level. But this Sunday, playing the steadily improving, veteran-laden Steelers within confines of Acrisure Stadium could be the Browns' toughest matchup to date. Pittsburgh improves to 4-0 at home and takes over first place in the AFC North at midseason. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Steelers 24, Browns 20 This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Browns 23, Steelers 20 The Browns have already beaten the Steelers once this season, and if they win this game, that would give them their first season sweep of Pittsburgh since 1988. That's right, it has somehow been 38 years since the Browns have swept the Steelers. The NFL should have flexed this game to Sunday night and asked everyone at the stadium to dress up like their favorite character from 1988. I would have definitely been John McClane from Die Hard, or maybe AC Slater. You know what? I'm not sure and we don't have time to talk about this. … (read more on CBS) Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Steelers 24, Browns 20 The Browns have all their five wins thanks to Deshaun Watson snatching victory from the jaws of defeat late in the fourth quarter. That's a feel-good development for rookie coach Todd Monken, but not sustainable as a first-place team. Aaron Rodgers is feeling it since the last Cleveland matchup and will outduel Watson with superior weapons. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Steelers 23, Browns 16 The Browns are 5-1 in one-score games – and their last six games have been decided by six points or less. Cleveland beat Pittsburgh in the first matchup, too. This time, Pittsburgh will build off the running game. The Steelers are 3-0 S/U at home, and Aaron Rodgers has a 101.6 passer rating.
