picks.headline: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game Curt Popejoy, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 6:36 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns square off, both teams at 5-2 and tied on top in the AFC North. The Steelers are looking for payback and the Browns are looking for their first sweep of the Steelers since 1988. Here are four bold predictions for this week's game. Jaylen Warren carries the offense The Browns run defense is struggling and Jaylen Warren is on a tear. Warren rushed for 93 yards in the first matchup and our bold prediction for Warren this week is he gets his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the year and tops 150 yards of total offense and two total touchdowns. T.J. Watt breaks out with 3 sacks This week is the perfect opportunity for T.J. Watt to quiet the critics as he faces backup right tackle Dawand Jones. Watt is currently fourth int he NFL with 5.5 sacks but has struggled with consistent pressure. This week he breaks out of his funk with a huge three-sack performance and one of them turns into a huge forced fumble. Pittsburgh solves their red zone woes with two scores For all the things he can do, head coach Mike McCarthy has struggled to get the Steelers red-zone offense on track. This is due in large part because he's been unwilling to just run the football near the goal line. That ends this week with two short rushing touchdowns. The Steelers currently have only one rushing touchdown all season. Double-digit win for the Steelers We appreciate what the Browns are building but Pittsburgh is at home and riding a three-game win streak since the loss to Cleveland and will keep it going with a double-digit win, bringing the Browns back to Earth about their place in the AFC North. Final score prediction: Steelers 35, Browns 24 This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game

picks.headline: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jarrett Bailey · SB Nation Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . away.headline: Cleveland Browns Practice Report for Thursday October 29 Week 8
away.blurb: Most notably, Browns defensive end Jared Verse (knee), who did not practice on Wednesday, was able to take part in a limited practice on Thursday. That's good news, as he absolutely has to be on the field for Sunday's game in Pittsburgh. After the Week 4 victory on a Thursday night, Verse endeared himself to Browns fans everywhere by trashing some of the Steelers players, calling them "dirty". He automatically gained likability among all Cleveland fans, as a result. Browns offensive tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) suffered a concussion in the Week 7 game against the Tennessee Titans, and he has not practiced this week in either session. That's the bad news. The good news is that he was the only 'DNP' for Thursday's practice. Rolling down the line, safety Grant Delpit (neck), defensive tackle Mason Graham (ankle), defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), cornerback Myles Harden (hamstring), center/offensive guard Elgton Jenkins (knee), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle), safety Daniel Thomas (ankle) and Verse were each limited participants on Thursday. After a limited practice on Thursday, running back Dylan Sampson (knee) was able to take part in a full practice session, and it appears he is trending toward another meaningful role in his second game back from the reserve/injured list. Gabriel was activated from the reserve/injured list, and he has been practicing in full for several weeks, as the Browns have figured out a way to keep all four quarterbacks without exposing any to the practice squad and/or having to lose them for the season on IR. home.headline: Thursday injury report for the Browns in Week 8 against the Steelers
home.blurb: Thursday provided major relief as two key starters upgraded from Wednesday's DNP list. Starting center Elgton Jenkins and rookie edge rusher Jared Verse both returned to the field in a limited capacity after sitting out Wednesday. They join safety Grant Delpit, interior defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., linebacker Carson Schwesinger, and defensive backs Myles Harden and Daniel Thomas, who all maintained their limited status. Sophomore running back Dylan Sampson upgraded from limited on Wednesday to a full participant on Thursday, clearing any lingering concerns regarding his knee as he looks to provide firepower to the Cleveland backfield. While no new players were added to the report, three key contributors earned upgrades, highlighted by edge rusher Jared Verse and center Elgton Jenkins returning to practice, and tailback Dylan Sampson taking another step forward. Here is Thursday's updated practice participation breakdown for Week 8. Right Tackle Tytus Howard (Concussion) Starting right tackle Tytus Howard was the lone absence on Thursday as he remains in concussion protocol. If he cannot clear the protocol by Sunday, we should expect Dawand Jones to start in his stead. Defensive Tackle Mason Graham (Ankle) Defensive Tackle Mike Hall Jr. (Ankle) Cornerback Myles Harden (Hamstring) Linebacker Carson Schwesinger (Ankle) Defensive Back Daniel Thomas (Ankle) Defensive End Jared Verse (Knee) Running Back Dylan Sampson (Knee) With 9 of the 10 listed players now practicing in some capacity, Friday's final report and game status designations will set the stage for Sunday's divisional battle in Pittsburgh. picks.headline: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions
picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to make a major statement in Week 8 when they travel to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Coming off an impressive victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta has a chance to carry that momentum into a divisional matchup with significant NFC South implications. The Buccaneers are coming off a blowout victory over the Carolina Panthers, but their 2-5 record leaves them needing a win to keep their divisional hopes alive. Meanwhile, a Falcons victory would give Atlanta sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Here is how the FalconsSI staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Scott Kennedy (3-4) This is the ultimate Lucy and Charlie Brown game for Falcons fans. Atlanta is coming off an impressive home victory against the San Francisco 49ers, while Tampa Bay remains just 2-5 despite a blowout win over Carolina. The opportunity is there for the Falcons to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South and potentially put the Buccaneers’ divisional hopes on life support. This is exactly the kind of game Atlanta should win. Unfortunately, it is also the type of game the Falcons have dropped year after frustrating year. However, looking beyond the history of disappointment, Atlanta is playing better football than Tampa Bay right now. The Falcons and Buccaneers can both run and stop the run, but Atlanta is getting better quarterback play and has a better set of (healthy) weapons on offense. Bucky Irvin is a great back, but Bijan Robinson is an elite player. The rainy weather might keep the score down in this one, and it could help negate the Falcon's advantage through the air. Surely, Lucy keeps the football in place for Charlie Brown this time. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 16 Gerald Thomas, III (3-4) Falcons-Buccaneers matchups always deliver compelling storylines, and Sunday’s meeting is no exception. There is Kevin Stefanski facing Baker Mayfield, Michael Penix Jr. making his long-awaited return to Tampa and Zac Robinson now serving as Atlanta’s offensive coordinator. Both teams enter the matchup following statement victories. Atlanta knocked off the previously undefeated 49ers, while Tampa Bay dominated the Panthers. A win would give the Falcons an opportunity to take over the top spot in the NFC South and continue building on their recent success. Prediction: Falcons 27, Buccaneers 17 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-4) 99% of Falcons fans have deep-seated trauma, and games like this are exactly why. The Falcons are fresh off a win against arguably the best team in football and are facing a team that’s struggling. These are exactly the games the Falcons have inexplicably lost in recent years. That said, this is not a one-sided matchup. The Buccaneers are much better than their record suggests. They have a really good defense and have been excellent in the trenches on both sides of the ball. On top of that, all of the Buccaneers’ losses have been one-score games against teams above .500. I think this game will come down to how the Falcons’ o-line fares against the Bucs’ d-line. Michael Penix Jr. is an above-average quarterback when he’s playing ahead of the sticks and has a clean pocket. The other question is whether this o-line can create running lanes against one of the best run-defending d-lines in the league. I’m much more confident in how the Falcons’ defense stacks up against the Bucs’ offense. The defensive line has been playing great, and the Bucs’ banged-up receiving corps is overmatched against the Falcons' secondary. Ultimately, I have the Falcons winning this, but I think it will be a closer matchup than most expect. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20 Darius Hayes (3-4) I expect a tough, physical divisional battle with the weather playing a major factor in Sunday’s outcome. The Falcons should lean heavily on their running game to control the clock, establish the pace and keep Tampa Bay’s offense off the field. Atlanta cannot afford to get away from what worked against San Francisco. Establishing the run will help take pressure off Penix while creating opportunities for the offense to control the game. Defensively, the Falcons need to make enough key stops and force the Buccaneers into difficult situations. Tampa Bay is capable of making plays offensively, but Atlanta has shown improvements on that side of the ball. Coming off last week’s momentum-building victory over the 49ers, I like the Falcons to carry that confidence into Tampa. It won’t be easy, but Atlanta does enough on both sides of the ball to earn a hard-fought divisional victory, take over first place in the NFC South, and leave Tampa Bay with a win. Prediction: Falcons 24, Buccaneers 17 Garrett Chapman (3-4) The Falcons are fresh off their biggest win of the season, but they have to take the show on the road on Sunday. They've had a lot of success in Tampa over the last few years, and this team will enter with a lot of confidence with how Michael Penix has been playing. This will be a tight game that I expect will come down to the final drive. The Buccaneer defense is solid, and it will be a difficult test on the road for an offense that hasn't shown it can consistently be a steady unit. Atlanta has a chance to take over the top spot in the NFC South on Sunday, but it won't happen just yet. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season. It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Falcons 24, Bucs 23 Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons. The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air. The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again. While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball. That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week. Overall Record: 4-3 James Hill, Writer: Falcons 21, Bucs 17 Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it. Overall Record: 3-4 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 24, Falcons 21 The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense. Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers. Logan Robinson, Founder: Bucs 28, Falcons 23 I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year. Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice. It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing. River Wells, Editor: Falcons 24, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way — Tampa Bay will have to go through the air. I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own — Bucs drop this one in Raymond James. Some of us believe the Bucs will keep the momentum going, while other writers think Tampa Bay will falter as it has multiple times this year. However, those surface numbers mask some serious flaws for the left-hander. According to PFF, Penix has seven big-time throws against eight turnover-worthy plays — and even more worrisome, he sports a 31% completion rate and a 10% turnover-worthy play rate when pressured. Both of those marks rank last in the NFL. Defensively, the Falcons ' run defense is a complete paper tiger. Everyone was talking about how dominant they were against the run early in the year, but look at the schedule. In the first four weeks, Atlanta looked good against the Steelers , Panthers , Packers , and Saints . But since Week 4, against tougher competition, the Falcons rank last in Rush EPA and 30th in Rush Success Rate. The Ravens rushed for 208 yards against them; the Bears rushed for 98 yards (with three touchdowns), and the 49ers rushed for 123 yards. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Preview: The Unluckiest Team in Football Tampa Bay might be the unluckiest team in the league. The Buccaneers are 1-5 in one-possession games against a brutal schedule, and they played three of those games with rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. Now, the Bucs are finally getting healthy defensively with Antoine Winfield Jr. and others potentially returning to the lineup. You can safely assume head coach Todd Bowles will dial up the heat on Atlanta, play press coverage on the outside to take away Penix's first read, and force him into mistakes under pressure. I trust this Tampa Bay defense, which ranks in the top five in DVOA against both the pass and the run. The Buccaneers are second in EPA per dropback and fifth in Rush EPA. If you want to stop Atlanta, you have to stop Bijan Robinson , and this Buccaneers defensive front has excelled at stopping the run for years. So, we are going to see them throw the kitchen sink at this crucial divisional home game. To avoid falling to 2-6, expect Todd Bowles to relentlessly pressure a quarterback in Michael Penix Jr. who grades out as the worst in the NFL when forced to navigate a collapsing pocket. away.blurb: Tampa Bay Buccaneers safety Antoine Winfield Jr. has missed three games thanks to a rib injury suffered against Green Bay in Week Four, but he is cleared to play on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons and expected to start. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, however, was ruled out on Friday and will be sidelined for the second game in a row by a foot injury. He had previously been listed with a concussion as well but was able to clear the league's concussion protocol late in the week. Tackle Luke Goedeke will also return to action after missing one game with a calf injury. Goedeke did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday but returned during Friday's session in a limited capacity. The Buccaneers and Falcons submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Eight meeting at Raymond James Stadium. The Buccaneers did not make any practice squad elevations this week and thus have 53 available players on Sunday, meaning they had to name five inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Falcons elevated linebacker Brian Asamoah and running back Khalil Herbert from their practice squad and therefore had to name seven players inactive for the game. Atlanta's offense will be without it's complementary backfield weapon for Bijan Robinson, as Brian Robinson is out due toa hamstring injury. Starting linebacker Divine Deablo will also miss the game due to a forearm injury, though fellow starter Kendal Daniels was cleared after missing some practice time due to an Achilles tendon ailment. Cornerback Billy Bowman will join Deablo on the sideline thanks to a hamstring strain, but cornerback Avieon Terrell, who was considered questionable for the game due to illness is good to go. away.headline: Falcons Have Another Lengthy Injury Report vs. Buccaneers, 1 Player Out Already
away.blurb: Falcons Have Another Lengthy Injury Report vs. Buccaneers, 1 Player Out Already Skip to main content SI.COM The Falcons officially ruled out running back Brian Robinson Jr. on Friday due to a hamstring injury, marking his second consecutive absence. Khalil Herbert will be his likely replacement after a good showing last week in a win over the 49ers. Robinson has not been able to return to the field since suffering the injury, leaving Atlanta without one of its primary options behind Bijan Robinson. While Robinson is the only player officially ruled out, the Falcons have several other injury concerns heading into Sunday’s divisional matchup. Eight players are listed as questionable, including three defensive players who could have significant roles against Tampa Bay. Defensive backs Billy Bowman Jr. and Avieon Terrell are both questionable. Bowman is dealing with a hamstring injury, while Terrell has been working through an illness. Both players missed Atlanta’s victory over San Francisco last week. Linebacker Divine Deablo is also questionable with a forearm injury. His potential absence would be notable for Atlanta’s defense, as Deablo has served as one of the unit’s primary communicators this season. The remaining questionable players include wide receivers Beaux Collins (hip) and Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder), defensive ends Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and Charles Snowden (back), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle). There is some encouraging news for Atlanta heading into the weekend. Collins and Williams both participated fully in Friday’s practice, while the other questionable players were limited participants. The Falcons have no players listed as doubtful. Falcons Rule Out Two Key Defensive Starters Ahead of Buccaneers Showdown The Atlanta Falcons will be without another key offensive player when they travel to Tampa to face the Buccaneers in Week 8. Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading the rushing attack, but losing another running back limits Atlanta’s depth at the position. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels stepped into a larger role against the 49ers and delivered one of the biggest performances of his young career. Daniels helped seal the victory with a late interception of Brock Purdy. Atlanta will need as many healthy players as possible against a Tampa Bay team coming off a convincing 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers. The Buccaneers enter Sunday’s matchup looking to build on that performance, while the Falcons are coming off a 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated 49ers. Atlanta and Tampa Bay will meet Sunday, Nov. 1, at Raymond James Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. Khalil Herbert will be his likely replacement after a good showing last week in a win over the 49ers. Robinson has not been able to return to the field since suffering the injury, leaving Atlanta without one of its primary options behind Bijan Robinson. While Robinson is the only player officially ruled out, the Falcons have several other injury concerns heading into Sunday’s divisional matchup. Eight players are listed as questionable, including three defensive players who could have significant roles against Tampa Bay. Defensive backs Billy Bowman Jr. and Avieon Terrell are both questionable. Bowman is dealing with a hamstring injury, while Terrell has been working through an illness. Both players missed Atlanta’s victory over San Francisco last week. Linebacker Divine Deablo is also questionable with a forearm injury. His potential absence would be notable for Atlanta’s defense, as Deablo has served as one of the unit’s primary communicators this season. The remaining questionable players include wide receivers Beaux Collins (hip) and Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder), defensive ends Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and Charles Snowden (back), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle). There is some encouraging news for Atlanta heading into the weekend. Collins and Williams both participated fully in Friday’s practice, while the other questionable players were limited participants. The Falcons have no players listed as doubtful. Falcons Rule Out Two Key Defensive Starters Ahead of Buccaneers Showdown The Atlanta Falcons will be without another key offensive player when they travel to Tampa to face the Buccaneers in Week 8. Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading the rushing attack, but losing another running back limits Atlanta’s depth at the position. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels stepped into a larger role against the 49ers and delivered one of the biggest performances of his young career. Daniels helped seal the victory with a late interception of Brock Purdy. Atlanta will need as many healthy players as possible against a Tampa Bay team coming off a convincing 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers. The Buccaneers enter Sunday’s matchup looking to build on that performance, while the Falcons are coming off a 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated 49ers. Atlanta and Tampa Bay will meet Sunday, Nov. 1, at Raymond James Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. away.headline: Colts cut veteran as injury report helps linebacker depth, hurts cornerbacks
away.blurb: Tight ends Tyler Warren (groin) and Drew Ogletree (knee) were both limited in practice for the second consecutive day. Warren, the team leader in receptions, has missed the last two weeks with the groin injury, and he was somewhat optimistic that he’ll be able to go against the Jaguars. News Sports Things To Do Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLTS Colts cut veteran as injury report helps linebacker depth, hurts cornerbacks Joel A. Erickson Indianapolis Star Oct. 29, 2026, 5:23 p.m. ET The Indianapolis Colts have made several roster changes due to injuries, particularly at cornerback and linebacker. Rookie linebacker CJ Allen is expected to start after recovering from an ankle injury, leading to the release of veteran Germaine Pratt. Cornerback Sauce Gardner returned to full practice, offering a potential solution to injuries in the secondary. INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts have made a flurry of roster moves this week, trying to cover a rash of injuries at the cornerback position while shoring up depth at linebacker. Rookie middle linebacker CJ Allen was a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day after missing last week’s game due to an ankle injury, although his fellow rookie, Bryce Boettcher, missed his second consecutive day with a groin injury. Indianapolis feels confident enough in its linebacker group to release veteran Germaine Pratt, who was signed to the practice squad two weeks ago but no longer has a path to playing time. Pratt played 20 snaps against Minnesota this week due to injuries, but the Colts plan to move Allen into the starting lineup now that he’s healthy. Pratt was a starter for 12 games in Indianapolis in 2025; the Colts are trying to get younger and faster at the position. “C.J. was going to start this week before he had that injury,” defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said. “I think they’re all putting their time in, and the more at bats they get, the better they’re going to be.” The Colts have larger issues at cornerback. Sauce Gardner practiced in full for the first time since suffering a calf injury against Tennessee, offering a potential starting option. Indianapolis placed Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve earlier this week, and Justin Walley missed the second consecutive day with a knee injury. The Jaguars have seen their safety group get hit with injuries at different points this season, and Merriweather has been one veteran who has helped steady the waters. The fourth-year safety signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2023 and appeared in 42 games with the Buccaneers in three seasons. This included 14 games with the Buccaneers in 2024 when Jaguars head coach Liam Coen was the team's offensive coordinator. “Need Kaevon to continue to step up and evolve. But being with him in Tampa, he was a guy that really helped on teams and played his tail off there but was also able to step in and he started, I think, like eight games for us that year in ‘24 at safety. The game wasn't too big for him," Coen said on Friday. Merriweather also spent time with the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions during parts of his career, and he signed to the Jaguars practice squad early in September. He was eventually moved up to the active roster, and he now looks like he will have to play a significant role in some facet against the Colts at home on Sunday. "And then when you went and watched him transition to Houston and then watched him throughout the preseason and the regular season on special teams, you could tell he took on some of the identity and ways in which Houston plays," Coen said. "That physicality, running to the football, burning it down and going and playing your ass off. That was something that was intriguing for us as well. And I've always just thought the game wasn't ever too big for Kaevon, never really got too high, too low. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings NBA Power Rankings Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. Safety Derwin James Jr., who's missed the Chargers' last three games with a nagging hamstring injury, now may be headed to injured reserve, head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday. What's wrong with Derwin James? As detailed by Elliott Teaford of the Orange County Register , the move to place James on IR isn't official yet, but Harbaugh said "it's looking like he may go to IR." Jun 17, 2026; El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James (3) during minicamp at The Bolt. It's a devastating blow for a team in desperate need of a spark, particularly given the expectations placed upon James this offseason. The Chargers rewarded James' elite play with a huge contract extension that made him the highest paid safety in the NFL for the second time in his career. Between James' injury and a struggling offense, though, the Chargers are now the last winless team in the NFL. What does Derwin James mean to the Chargers? So far this season, James' stats haven't exactly jumped off the page. In his three games, he had 21 tackles and broke up a pass. Those numbers, though, belie a spectacular resume thus far. Nov 30, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James Jr. (3) reacts against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Over his career, which includes parts or all of eight seasons, he has 12 interceptions, 47 passes broken up, six forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries and 19 sacks, according to Football Reference . In the six seasons in which he's played at least 14 games, he's been a Pro Bowler five times and an All Pro four times. That kind of production and experience is impossible to replace, and this Sunday, Matthew Stafford and the Rams might have a field day with the Bolts defense. Considering the Rams are also looking to rebound from a poor start to the year, this battle for LA supremacy might be the defining week for both franchises. Additionally, Awosika, Thompson, and Leonard did not practice all week so head coach Jim Harbaugh and the coaching staff knew that they would be without those three players as well, which like James should not have affected the game plan too much. Lastly, for Mack to be available is not a surprise at all, as he was simply resting, and as a veteran, that is fairly normal for Mack so he should be a full go against the Rams' offensive line on Sunday. So, when the game starts on Sunday, it will be interesting to see if the Chargers can come out and have a full 60-minute performance to earn their first win of the year or if the Chargers' struggles will continue and lead to a Rams win as well as the Chargers falling to 0-7. This week, he reportedly had a setback, and as a result, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he's a candidate to go on injured reserve. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) also won't play. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, both of whom have hamstring injuries, are questionable for Sunday's contest. Garrett will be out on Sunday, as will wide receiver Davante Adams. At times, the Rams have struggled defensively — they gave up 302 passing yards last week against the Las Vegas Raiders — so perhaps there is a slight opening for the Bolts to find some success. The most immediate thing that would help is for them to become healthier. Starting right tackle Joe Alt hasn't played since Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks due to a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a concussion during L.A.'s last game, which was a 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6, and he entered concussion protocol as a result. Both men returned to practice for the Chargers this week, and there is good news about their status for this Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. Alt and McConkey are on the mend In the Chargers' final injury report for Sunday's game, neither Alt nor McConkey are listed, which means both are expected to play, per Noah Furtado of The Athletic. While the Chargers are 0-6 and have been a disaster, the Rams haven't exactly lived up to expectations either. The Rams have a 3-4 record despite being strong favorites to win the Super Bowl championship when the season started, and while they have had some injuries, such as the one that reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is dealing with, they have their own problems. The Bolts currently rank last in the NFL in points per game, 28th in passing yards and last in turnovers. Quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions heading into Week 8 with eight, against just five touchdown passes. home.blurb: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday's game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful. Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday. Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well. Additionally, Parkinson didn't participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game. Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington's back locked up in practice, which is why he'll be listed as questionable. On the Chargers' side, they'll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Replicating that performance is going to be much easier said than done in the rematch, however, especially with Andy Reid's team hitting the road. Denver seems to be finding its stride just a little bit, although a win over the Arizona Cardinals won't convince anyone that the reigning division champions are all the way back. The winner of Sunday's tilt could generate some serious momentum in the AFC West race as the season approaches its midpoint. What gives in the afternoon window of play? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 8 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: For the second week in a row, I'm expecting a low-scoring game. This time, however, I think the Chiefs will find the end zone. Kansas City just needs enough from Rashee Rice and his fellow pass catchers to allow Kenneth Walker to have opportunities similar to the ones he took advantage of in Week 1. The final inactives list will be massive for both teams, but I expect the Chiefs to escape Denver with a narrow win. Jordan Foote: Getting wideout Rashee Rice back in the fold for this one is huge. Given that Xavier Worthy's come back down to earth, Travis Kelce is banged up and Kenneth Walker III has finally looked human, having a formidable weapon on offense is paramount. On the other side of the ball, missing cornerback Mansoor Delane will hurt, but being minus L'Jarius Sneed might just be an addition-by-subtraction scenario. Expect a one-score game that is far from the prettiest, albeit with Kansas City still doing enough to complete the sweep of Denver and maintain first place in the AFC West. Joshua Schulman: The Chiefs are reeling after an ugly loss to Seattle in prime time last week. It’s difficult to imagine the offense looking any more inept than it did a week ago when it mustered just one field goal all night. The Broncos’ defense isn’t quite as dominant as Seattle’s but still is a formidable unit. With that said, we saw who the better team was when these two sides met in Week 1. Denver has been winning in spite of Bo Nix’s play, not because of it, and the KC coaching staff has to have stressed the importance of a game in which it could lose the first-place lead in the AFC West. Tyler Brown: This feels like a tighter game than Week 1, but the Chiefs' strengths match up well against those of the Broncos. Denver will be desperate with the divisional stakes swinging so heavily. With Jonathan Cooper lined up opposite Nik Bonitto, the Broncos have a better edge-rush pairing than they did in September, which puts the Chiefs’ tackle situation under real stress if it ends up in too many obvious dropback situations. The Broncos may perform better this go-around, but the matchup tilts toward the Chiefs. Denver’s rushing defense ranks 28th and leads the league in missed tackles, which is exactly the situation Kenneth Walker thrives in. Getting Rashee Rice back is a bigger deal than it may sound, because it gives Patrick Mahomes another reliable weapon and it lets Xavier Worthy and the rest of the group settle into their roles. On the other side, Denver is 30th in total offense and 25th in scoring, and Nix has struggled when pressured, especially against the blitz. If Steve Spagnuolo gets creative and some pass rushers outside of George Karlaftis step up, that is another major Chiefs advantage. The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training. Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak. The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule. How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires. Pick : Broncos 26, Chiefs 24 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 5-2 : Last week's game was fairly easy to predict if you've watched this team long enough. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time? Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 19 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 5-2 : It’s hard to predict what the Broncos will do this week with Zach Allen, Jaylen Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga all injured . This game may come down to which team is healthier. However, I expect a redemptive effort by the Broncos' defense after the embarrassment Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs put on them in Week 1. It was also against the Chiefs at Mile High when Nix turned the corner last season. Ultimately, it's an ugly one, but a win for Denver against the Chiefs, who lack pop offensively outside of Walker Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17 Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 5-2 : The Broncos were not good in Week 1 but have played better since. away.headline: Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 Final injury report: Rashee Rice returning
away.blurb: Cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) was listed as questionable after suddenly missing practice Thursday and Friday. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that it is the same shoulder he has dealt with injuries to since training camp and forced him to miss time in Weeks 1 and 2. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee) was listed as questionable after limited participation in practice for two days and missing on Wednesday with an NIR/personal designation. He is regularly listed as a limited participant due to a lingering knee issue. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was ruled out after three days of limited participation in practice; he was designated to return from the Physically Unable to Perform list on Wednesday . He will continue working in the 21-day practice window before the Chiefs must sign him to the active 53-man roster. Defensive end R Mason Thomas (personal) was listed as questionable after missing practice on Friday. On Friday, Andy Reid said Thomas will meet the Chiefs in Denver and will likely play. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) did not have a game status listed after improving to full participation in practice on Friday; he hasn’t played since tweaking his hamstring in Week 4, but he should be making his return to the field in Denver. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) did not have a game status listed and practiced in full on Friday after being labeled a limited participant in practice on Thursday. He banged up his ankle in the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was ruled out after missing practice all week; he hasn’t played since leaving the Week 5 win over the Los Angeles Chargers with an ankle injury. This season, he is tied for the team lead with two interceptions — one he returned for a touchdown — and has three passes defended, one forced fumble and three tackles for loss. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) was listed as questionable after limited practice on Thursday and Friday; he suffered his injury in the Week 7 win over the Arizona Cardinals . Pro Bowl defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring) was listed as questionable after two limited practices to end the week following an absence from Wednesday’s practice. Allen has 4.5 sacks this year and hasn’t missed any time for this injury so far. After having no designation on Wednesday, running back RJ Harvey (knee) was limited on Thursday, then didn’t practice on Friday and has been ruled out . He has 304 total yards and two touchdowns this season. Starting safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) was listed as questionable after two limited practices to end the week; Jones intercepted Mahomes in Week 1 and has the second-most tackles on Denver’s defense this season. Left tackle Garrett Bolles (hip) is questionable to play after limited participation in practice all week. Bolles hasn’t missed a snap for Denver so far this season, but he was not listed on the injury report last week. Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 Final injury report: Rashee

Denver is also dealing with several injuries, including two players ruled out and four listed as questionable. Safety Taylor Rapp is expected to continue filling in for Hufanga, who could return in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers . Denver also listed four players as questionable: Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle — chest Safety Brandon Jones — hamstring Left tackle Garett Bolles — hip Defensive end Zach Allen — hamstring All four players participated in a limited capacity during Friday's practice. away.headline: Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns
away.blurb: The Chiefs downgraded rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane to out with a shoulder injury, and the Chiefs have also placed cornerback L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve, according a report from Charean Williams of Pro Football Talk and multiple other outlets. Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL What MLB's labor proposal means Chiefs Lose Two Cornerbacks To Injury As Key Receiver Returns Bob McCullough · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 1, 2026 at 12:24 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs secondary just got a lot thinner, but they're getting a key receiver back for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos. On offense, the news is about receiver Rashee Rice, who will be back in the lineup according to a report from Nate Taylor of ESPN. Rice will be returning from a hamstring injury he sustained against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. Rice was able to participate in every practice this week, per reports, and he currently has 13 receptions on 16 targets for 190 yards and a touchdown. As for the two cornerbacks, Delane is the more serious injury by far. The rookie was Kansas City's top draft choice with the No. 6 pick in the draft, and his shoulder has been an issue since OTAs. He wore a non-contact jersey for most of the summer, but Delane was able to get back on the field for the Chiefs' opener against the Denver Broncos, and he had a big interception in Kansas City's 31-10 romp. But Delane has been on and off the injury report for weeks now with this same issue, so the news isn't exactly surprising. What was surprising, though, was coach Andy Reid revealing that the injury was a hairline fracture of his scapula. His stat line at the moment includes 27 tackles, an interception and five passes defended in five games this season. Sneed's situation is very different. He returned to Kansas City during the summer after a failed stint with the Tennessee Titans. His injury designation was personal/knee, but the personal part of this is new if there's anything substantial to it. Sneed played well early, but he was badly exposed in Kansas City's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night. The Seahawks picked on Sneed for most of the night, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba especially had some strong moments against the former Chiefs star. The Chiefs have also signed cornerback Melvin Smith to the active roster from the practice squad, and they activated defensive end Tyreke Smith from the practice squad to the game-day roster. Kansas City is 5-1 going into Sunday's contest at Denver, which is 5-2. with the two teams battling for the lead in the AFC West.

The Kansas City Chiefs have released their final injury report for Week 8's matchup with the Denver Broncos. He'll meet us there in Denver.” While Delane's status remains up in the air, the Chiefs did have some positive injury news to report on offense. Reid expressed optimism that WR Rashee Rice (hamstring) would return to the starting lineup after missing the past two weeks. Rice carries no game status designation for Sunday. With that in mind, I asked the following question this past week: What are your predictions, bold or otherwise, for the Miami Dolphins' defense and offense in this coming Sunday's game vs. the New England Patriots? Who do you expect to lead the team in key categories like tackles, tackles for loss, pass breakups, interceptions, defensive touchdowns, etc., on defense, and receiving yards, touchdowns, receptions, rushing production, and first downs, etc., on offense? What are your stat-line projections for our key playmakers this week, and/or who will be the team's MVPs on each side of the ball? Below are some of your takes and predictions for tomorrow's game- DalFinsFan is rightfully curious about this oddity in the schedule that seemingly helps a team from a colder climate that just happens to be the Pats. Curious why this is a late game instead of a 1:00pm ko. dedstrk says make it mistake-free and maybe? We need mistake free football and for the Pats to not take the Dolphins seriously enough for most of the game. Run the ball and continue on with the explosives and running the ball for first downs with Malik and OG. Phinette says the route to victory is keeping the ball out of the Pats' offense's hands. Our best shot at pulling off the upset is by controlling the clock. We need to stick with our ground game and avoid the costly three and outs. On defense we have to avoid being torched by the deep ball. If we can force the Pats to grind it out we have a shot. Phoenix6 has Miami narrowly edging out NE for victory #2. Dolphins 🐬 28, Patriots 27. coluccim believes that bad weather would be our best friend on Sunday. Our pass D is god awful, really. Pray for rain Phins1972 is much more focused on the rookies' development across the roster over the final score. I really wish there were a young edge rusher on the roster who looked like a legitimate developmental piece. I'm still not a believer in Chop Robinson. He's played better lately, and credit where it's due, but I'm not sold yet. I'm interested to see whether Caleb Douglas can build on his recent performance and make an impact again. It would also be encouraging to see Chris Bell put together a solid outing. On the ground, I'd love to see Ollie top 100 yards once more. If Miami gets one of those hot, humid afternoons, a big back consistently moving the chains could have Patriots defenders gasping for air by the fourth quarter. If they can keep the game reasonably competitive, that'll be a positive. At this stage, player development is every bit as important as the final score, if not more so. Bill Hazlett has the defense doing their job well enough tomorrow to give us the W. Defense holds up. 28-17 Fins! JUK has Miami dropping this one by double digits. The Pats are clearly a stronger roster top to bottom. I think we will need to win the turnover battle to have a chance which has been the pats weakness but if Maye keep things clean they should win. It's likely to be a tough day for Willis if they get ahead too, as their secondary is so much stronger than our receiver room. We need to keep it close and run the ball well to have a chance. I'll say pats by 10 finfanfromsiam points to this team's long-standing issue covering any decent TEs. Does NE have TEs?? Nuff said…… CluelessNFLfan says that reality sets back in with another loss. The Phins come back down to earth this week. Pats 24, Phins 17. Robert Burstein has Miami losing by two TD's. I do think Miami can keep this game a little close until half time, but overall I think D.Maye will have a big game passing and making plays running. I've got Miami losing 13-27. Jptapt is being positive. Molly Polly II sees another upset on the horizon. I'm calling for an upset…why not! Patriots are favored +7.5. Defense tightens up shot group, Ollie beast mode another 100+ yards. Malik playing at home, confident, ready to prove he's the guy who can lead this team. Huge upset, Finz win with seconds left on the clock, 26-24! 🐬🐬 Gusman says it might be close, or Maye might just make the Dolphins' secondary look silly. If Drake Maye plays as he has for the past 4 games he should carve up the Dolphins secondary. Miami should be able to limit the Pats run game. Pats will attempt to shutdown Miamis run game forcing the Dolphins into passing situations. The Pats have a much better secondary than the Phins. Best bet for Miami is to hope Maye is sloppy and throws a couple picks and loses a fumble or two. The Pats are coming off a 10 day break and are not taking a Miami victory for granted. Should be a fairly close entertaining game. Well, the vote is split, with some of us agreeing with Vegas that the Dolphins are clearly set up for another loss, while others are feeling a bit more positive after pulling out the win last weekend against the NY Jets. home.blurb: Injury Report Analysis: WR A.J. Brown, RB TreVeyon Henderson questionable for Week 8 matchup vs. the Dolphins Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Brown (ankle/knee) is officially questionable for Sunday's game after sitting out the final two practices this week. On Friday, New England listed WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable for Week 8. On the one hand, the Patriots haven't ruled out any players as their active roster gets healthier. However, several key contributors remain on injured reserve (WR Mack Hollins, WR Romeo Doubs, LG Aijah Vera-Tucker, RG Mike Onwenu), while Brown's participation decreasing as the practice week wore on was a noteworthy development. While still managing his recovery from a high-ankle sprain, Brown's knee reportedly "flared up" in practice this week, which landed him on Wednesday's injury report as limited. Brown then didn't participate in Thursday or Friday's session, but the 29-year-old still has a chance to play on Sunday. The Pats top wideout has caught just 6-of-16 targets for 75 receiving yards in two games since returning from injury. On Friday, head coach Mike Vrabel had an update on Brown's status. As for the offensive line, the Patriots are managing injuries there, too. Starting RT Morgan Moses continues to play through a foot injury while C/G Ben Brown is pushing to get back into the lineup. Brown started three games at right guard before exiting the Patriots Week 6 win over the Jets with a knee injury. Brown was a full participant in practice this week, suggesting he could return to the starting lineup. Moving over to the defense, the positive injury news is that the Patriots secondary is expected to be whole for the first time since Week 3. Although he's officially questionable, CB Carlton Davis III (neck) is trending toward playing on Sunday after participating in full for all three practices this week. Davis has missed three straight games and four of the last six contests due to his neck injury, while top CB Christian Gonzalez has also missed time with a shoulder injury. "Yeah, I mean, it's everything," Gonzalez said of Davis's return. "CD is a great vet. Somebody that I lean on a lot, able to talk to, pick his mind about certain things. He's seen a lot of balls, so just having him back out there is amazing. Excited to get all of us back." Although the wide receiver situation is in flux, the Patriots roster health is trending in the right direction, with OL Ben Brown and CB Carlton Davis III expected to return this week. The next steps for New England are practice squad elevations and downgrades en route to Miami on Saturday. Brown, who is dealing with both an ankle and knee injury. The Eagles have lost Jalen Hurts for the season due to a blood clot, putting Tanner McKee in the starting quarterback position for the foreseeable future. The Eagles have been banged up across the board this season, but especially on offense with DeVonta Smith (out in Week 8) and Saquon Barkley both missing time. That’s led to the Eagles ranking in the bottom five in the league in EPA/Play on offense, and it puts them as underdogs in this divisional matchup against the Commanders. Washington lost star receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season in Week 6, but it's coming off a bye and still has a chance to make a play for the top spot in the NFC East. Daniels was dealing with a dislocated elbow, has played in the last two games – and played well – despite making a critical mistake in overtime in a tie against the New York Giants. If the Commanders don’t turn things around sooner rather than later, there’s a good chance Dan Quinn could be coaching for his job. All week long, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player prop selections, and much more for this NFC East rivalry matchup. Here’s a compilation of some of our favorites to get you ready for Eagles vs. Commanders on Sunday night. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Eagles vs. Commanders Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Philadelphia Eagles +6 (-110) vs. Washington Commanders – Iain MacMillan Jayden Daniels OVER 202.5 Passing Yards (-112) – Peter Dewey Dallas Goedert Anytime TD (+220) – Peter Dewey Stefon Diggs Anytime TD (+215) – Peter Dewey Ahead of Week 8, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s taking the points with the Eagles: I'm going to hope that Saquon Barkley is healthy enough to play in this game, because if he is, the Eagles will have a path to cover the spread. The Commanders' run defense has been bad this season, ranking 31st in opponent rush success rate, meaning the Eagles should be able to run the ball against them. I still think the Eagles have enough skill on offense to compete with a bad Commanders team, so I'm not ready to lay the points on Washington. I'll back the Eagles as underdogs for a second straight week. Philly has struggled a bit against the pass, ranking 28th in passing yards allowed, in the bottom 10 in passing touchdowns allowed and 25th in EPA/Pass. That’s a great sign for Jayden Daniels, who had his best game of the season throwing the ball in Week 6 against San Francisco. The star quarterback threw for 300 yards and completed 72.5 percent of his passes in a close loss in primetime. He had just 164 passing yards against Philly in Week 1, but Daniels has been much more effective since coming back from a dislocated elbow, combining for over 300 passing and rushing yards in back-to-back games. He’s worth a look on Sunday night with so many other star players banged up. Earlier this season, Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert had four catches for 77 yards and two scores in a Week 1 win over Washington. He has not found the end zone since, but the veteran tight end has remained a big part of the offense. Over the last two weeks with McKee at quarterback, Goedert has been targeted 15 times, catching 11 passes for 109 yards. That workload should eventually turn into some scores, and this is a great matchup for the Eagles tight end to make it happen. Through six games, the Commanders have allowed eight receiving scores to the tight end position. Only the Detroit Lions (10) have allowed more. Goedert is a great bet to lead an otherwise banged up Philadelphia offense in Week 8. Stefon Diggs has four touchdown catches in five appearances in the 2026 season for the Commanders, and he’s now the No. 1 receiver with McLaurin done for the year. Diggs has played just 59.8 percent of the Commanders’ snaps on offense, yet he’s been targeted at least six times in every game. That’s led to 24 receptions for 214 yards, and Jayden Daniels has thrown the ball Diggs’ way a ton this season. My Eagles vs. Commanders predictions see a Sunday Night Football shootout in spite of the low total on the board. The Week 8 battle of the NFC East basement pits the Philadelphia Eagles against the Washington Commanders (-5.5) on Sunday, Nov. 1. This division has been a mess in the first two months of the schedule, but this one could go a long way toward defining the second half of the season. Here are my favorite NFL picks for tonight's game, led by the Over. TOP PICK Eagles vs Commanders prediction: Over 40.5 If you read my weekly NFL Underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. A big reason why is this underrated offense. Yes, Philadelphia has a backup under center and is potentially missing its top two WRs again. Yet, the Eagles have looked capable with Tanner McKee at the wheel. And with Saquon Barkley back, they went blow-for-blow with the Cowboys for 45 minutes on Monday until running out of ammo in the final frame. The Washington Commanders defense doesn't put up much of a fuss. Washington is a bottom-tier team in several key defensive measurements , including third-down conversions and red-zone defense. Making up for the soft stop unit is an offense that should at least be able to keep its quarterback clean. Philadelphia's once-vaunted pass rush is no more, boasting the fifth-lowest pressure rate , and that means Jayden Daniels has time in the pocket. Daniels is now four weeks returned from his elbow injury, with a bye in Week 7, and is coming off his best performance of the season. He passed for 300 yards and 72.5% completion rate with two TDs in a loss to the 49ers on Oct. 19. With both defenses leaking, there should be plenty of points, and you'll find more totals ideas in our Week 8 Over/Under predictions .
