away.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.blurb: Commanders receiver Treylon Burks was designated as questionable to play Sunday night's game against the Philadelphia Eagles due to a foot injury. That's especially notable for Washington's first game without Terry McLaurin, who suffered a season-ending torn patellar tendon against the 49ers in a Week 6 loss heading into a bye. Burks was among four Commanders listed as questionable on the official Commanders injury report, which was released on Friday. Tight end John Bates (shoulder), defensive lineman Johnny Newton (pectoral) — he's technically still on IR — and defensive tackle Daron Payne (foot) are also questionable. home.headline: Washington Commanders, Eagles Release Final SNF Injury Reports
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders will enter Sunday night with a largely healthy roster available. After being held out during the week and trending toward an inactive for the first time this season, defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw has officially been ruled out for the Sunday night meeting against the Philadelphia Eagles. Kinlaw was sidelined due to a knee injury suffered during the week six loss against the San Francisco 49ers, ruling him out midway through the game in the latest blow to the defensive line's depth. Yet the Commanders may be able to replenish Newton's role in the rotation as defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton looks to make his season debut. After tearing his pectoral muscle during preseason , the Commanders began the week by opening his 21 day practice window with Newton listed as questionable on the team's injury report released on Friday. Newton is one of four Commanders to draw the questionable tag alongside tight end John Bates, wide receiver Treylon Burks and defensive tackle Daron Payne. The latter marked a surprise after being listed as limited in Friday's practice with a foot injury, the first time the veteran has drawn an injury tag all week. Payne also found himself among the top trade candidates across the NFL earlier in the week with the week eight primetime divisional matchup a chance for the rest of the depth to step up in his absence. Bates has been sidelined through the week before being limited with a shoulder injury in Friday's practice. Burks, meanwhile, was limited on both Wednesday and Friday as he battles back from the foot injury suffered in the fourth quarter against the Niners. Wide receiver Stefon Diggs, meanwhile, was a full participant the rest of the week, as expected, after drawing a rest day on Wednesday. The Eagles, however, will enter Sunday short-handed after ruling out both wide receivers Dontayvion Wicks and DeVonta Smith, leaving rookie Makai Lemon to shoulder the load in the room amid questions surrounding a passing attack led by Tanner McKee. He will have a key piece to lean on with running back Saquon Barkley available to play after battling through hamstring and back injuries ahead of the matchup. Barkley was not spotted at practice by Eagles' media through the week until Friday, leaving a question as to how healthy he will be for week eight. The Eagles also ruled out linebacker Jihaad Campbell, wide receiver Britain Covey and cornerback Jonathan Jones. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Bears take their surging offense into Seattle for a matchup with one of the NFL's best defenses Getty Images In the Week 8 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Seattle Seahawks host the Chicago Bears . Seattle enters this game fresh off a victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs , snapping a two-game losing skid. The Seahawks' defense is settling in and once again looks like one of the best units in the league, but faces one of its toughest tests of the season on Monday night. Chicago enters having won both of its games since starting quarterback Caleb Williams returned from injury, improving to 5-2 in the process. The Bears have looked like one of the best offenses in the NFL whenever Williams has been on the field, but they, too, face arguably their toughest test of the season on Monday evening. Will Seattle make it back-to-back wins, or will the Bears ruin their evening with a road upset? How to watch Seahawks vs. Bears live Date: Monday, Nov. 2 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lumen Field (Seattle) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -3, O/U 46.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bears have the ball Chicago has scored, 59, 31 and 30 points in the three Caleb Williams starts that were not played against the Minnesota Vikings in a driving rainstorm. The Bears piled up 552, 368 and 405 yards in those three games, and turned the ball over only twice in those contests. For the season (including the game against Minnesota), Williams has completed 71% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt, both of which are career-high figures. He has thrown five touchdowns against one interception and rushed 24 times for 128 yards and two additional scores. Williams has generally thrown short passes, with an average depth of throw of only 7.0 yards, according to Tru Media. Despite that, he has created explosive passing plays at the third-highest rate in the league (10.7% of dropbacks). That's thanks in large part to the fact that the Bears are averaging 6.4 yards after catch per completion on his throws, the fourth-best mark in the league. The Seahawks, though, limit YAC as well as just about any team in football. They've allowed only 4.5 yards after catch per completion, which ranks third-best in the NFL. They play shell coverages a lot of the time, and they rally to the ball and tackle as well in the secondary as anybody. Their defensive backs and linebackers rarely miss opportunities to bring ball-carriers to the ground. The Bears generally want to run the ball more often than almost any team in the league, with a 48.7% rush rate, according to Tru Media. The Seahawks are elite at stopping the run, however, as we saw last week against Kenneth Walker III . D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson will have their work cut out for them here, even against a defense that plays a lot of nickel and dime and doesn't load the box. The Chicago offensive line will have to do a lot of work to move Seattle's defensive front off the ball, which has proven extremely difficult for opposing lines this year. When the Seahawks have the ball Seattle's offense is built almost entirely around the exploits of superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba . JSN leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards, 43 receiving first downs and eight receiving touchdowns. He has been targeted on 36.3% of the team's pass attempts, which ranks as the No. 1 mark in the NFL. So does his 33.9% targets-per-route-run rate, which is narrowly ahead of CeeDee Lamb's . Smith-Njigba has more receptions than the next three closest players on the Seahawks: AJ Barner , Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed combined for 53. His 867 yards are also considerably more than the 562 that trio has combined as well. They are ancillary pieces at best, and typically they are scarcely involved in the offense. Shaheed is also out on Monday night, which means the secondary options will be even more limited than usual. The Bears, like everyone else in the league, do not have anyone who can cover Smith-Njigba. It's not possible. The best chance to limit him is to get to Sam Darnold and force hurried decisions that lead to turnovers. Darnold, despite missing time due to injury, leads the NFL with eight interceptions. Under pressure, he has been dreadful, completing only 26 of 66 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and four picks. He ranks second-to-last in the league in EPA per dropback on pressured plays, per Tru Media. If the Bears can get into his face, they can force him into mistakes and flip the game on its head. Something that will help them in that effort is the arrival of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who is a game wrecker on the interior. Simmons is among the league leaders in both pressures and sacks when lined up inside. He'll have to deal with what is now one of the best guard duos in the league in Quenton Nelson and Grey Zabel , and Simmons could also see his snaps limited in his first game with his new team. (Nelson is likely to play a full complement in his Seattle debut, given how reluctant teams are to rotate offensive linemen.) The Seattle running game should get a boost from the expected returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price . Charbonnet hasn't played all season after tearing his ACL during last year's Super Bowl run, while Price has been out since Week 3 with a chest injury. The combination of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has largely been ineffective, and even if Charbonnet and Price can generate slightly below-average efficiency, they'll represent an improvement over the incumbent duo. The Bears have given up an average of 4.4 yards per carry this season, which ranks 23rd in the league. Seattle's defense is looking like the unit we expected it to be coming into the year. The Seahawks just shut down Kenneth Walker last week; they should be able to do the same to D'Andre Swift. That puts the entire game on Williams' right shoulder. He can handle that, of course, but it's incredibly difficult to do against Mike Macdonald's unit. That's especially true if the Seahawks get Price and Charbonnet back in the lineup at running back and can run the ball with some degree of success. Pick the Seahawks to take care of business at home. Both of these teams are currently in the wild card mix in the NFC, and while they both want to win their respective divisions, having the tiebreaker in the head-to-head meeting could go a long way for their playoff hopes. Sam Darnold and the Seahawks are coming off a huge win over the Kansas City Chiefs in primetime in Week 7, and they have the No. 2 defense in the NFL in EPA/Play (No. 1 in yards per play allowed) through seven weeks. Meanwhile, the Bears had a mini bye after a Thursday night win in Week 7, and they’re 5-2 overall with three wins in four starts by former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams. The Bears star is firmly in the mix to win the MVP award this season, and he’s looking to throw for 300 yards for the third game in a row. Can he make it happen against this elite Seattle defense? Oddsmakers have set the defending champs as favorites at home on Monday night, but the Bears have won and covered in every game that Williams has started and finished this season. In the leadup to Week 8, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player prop selections and more for the Bears vs. Seahawks battle. With so much at stake in this NFC showdown, here’s a compilation of our favorite bets for this matchup on Monday night. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Bears vs. Seahawks Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chicago Bears Moneyline (+148) vs. Seattle Seahawks – Iain MacMillan Rome Odunze UNDER 3.5 Receptions (-170) – Peter Dewey Jaxon Smith-Njigba Longest Reception OVER 29.5 Yards (-112) – Iain MacMillan Colston Loveland Anytime TD (+220) – Peter Dewey Earlier this week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for every game in Week 8 in his Road to 272 column , and he’s taking the Bears as his upset of the week: I'm ready to believe in the Chicago Bears. Ben Johnson is clearly the real deal as head coach, and Caleb Williams has improved significantly since last season. Last season, he ranked 39th out of 45 starting quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected. This season, he ranks first at +9.0%. The Bears' defense has also been better than people expected this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in opponent success rate. I still have some concerns surrounding the Seattle offense. It did enough to beat the Chiefs last week, but their running game is still weak, and Sam Darnold hasn't been as efficient as he was a year ago. I'll take the Bears as my upset pick of the week. Former first-round pick Rome Odunze has played a big role for the Bears this season, catching 24 of his 38 targets for 381 yards while playing 84.9 percent of the team’s offensive snaps. However, he only has two games this season with more than three receptions, and he’s been targeted seven or fewer times in six of his seven appearances. With that usage, I’m going to fade Odunze on Monday against a Seattle defense that is No. 2 in the NFL in EPA/Pass through seven weeks. Odunze doesn’t have nearly a big enough target share in Ben Johnson’s offense to trust to have one of his best games of the season against this elite defense. All season long, MacMillan shares his top-10 props of the week in his Player Prop Countdown , and JSN is the No. 7 selection for Week 8: The Bears' secondary has been susceptible to giving up explosive plays through the air this season. They have given up nine receptions of 40+ yards, which is two more than any other team has given up. They've also allowed 21 completions of 20+ yards. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba almost certainly being a player that's going to be targeted early and often in this game, I'm willing to bet on him hauling in at least one pass of 30+ yards. Caleb Williams is back, and so is second-year tight end Colston Loveland. The former Michigan star has scored in back-to-back games for the Bears, catching 13 of his 19 targets during that stretch. Loveland got off to a slow start in 2026, but there’s no doubt that Williams loves the young tight end in the red zone. Loveland has a tough matchup against a Seattle defense that has allowed just 241 yards and two scores to the position this season, but he’s been too involved over the last two weeks to pass up at north of 2/1. away.headline: Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks
away.blurb: The Seahawks will be without at least three players for Monday night's game against the Bears, with left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) all ruled out due to injury. Additionally, outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu is doubtful due to an ankle injury that kept him off the practice field all week. On a positive note, running back Zach Charbonnet does not have a game status and head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Charbonnet will play Monday, marking his return from a torn ACL suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs. home.headline: Seahawks’ Week 8 injury report vs. Bears: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price set to return for MNF clash
home.blurb: Seahawks’ Week 8 injury report vs. Bears: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price set to return for MNF clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL What MLB's labor proposal means Alex House, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Mon, November 2, 2026 at 5:08 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads It is quite easy to blame the Seattle Seahawks ' uneven first half on an inefficient run game, but the defending Super Bowl champions did not exactly post eye-popping numbers on the ground during the 2025 regular season. They averaged 4.1 yards per carry and ranked 11th in the league with 123.3 rushing yards per week. Though, even when the backfield was lacking firepower, it still posed a threat to defenses. The 2026 Seahawks are hoping to get that back on Monday. Emanuel Wilson has done his best to shoulder the burden following Kenneth Walker III's free-agency departure and multiple injuries to the position group, eclipsing 80 rushing yards on three separate occasions. He can use some help, though. An incoming future Hall of Fame offensive lineman like Quenton Nelson should provide a huge boost , but a versatile RB room is an important element of many successful teams. And Seattle (4-3) is ready to shake things up a bit. Zach Charbonnet is expected to make his season debut versus the Chicago Bears , and although he is still on injured reserve at time of print, rookie Jadarian Price is in line to join him. The former is returning from a torn ACL he suffered in the playoffs back in January, and the latter logged full practice participation on Friday after missing the last month of action with a chest injury. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bears are inserting All-Pro defensive tackle and big midseason acquisition Jeffery Simmons into their front seven, so the Seahawks may have a better chance of keeping Chicago on its toes with their top-three ball-carriers. Fans have seen what quarterback Sam Darnold can accomplish when Seattle establishes its ground attack. Even without Kyle Monangai, who is still battling turf toe and a thumb injury, the Bears boast a dangerous D'Andre Swift-led rushing unit. The Seahawks must close the gap in that crucial area on Monday night. Their chances of doing so have seemingly improved. Opening kickoff will commence at 8:15 p.m. ET.
